Abstract excerpt: Dense-caption retrieval has recently been improved by introducing segmentation, edge maps, LLM-filtered captions, and cross-modal modules into contrastive fine-tuning. However, these methods largely inherit the same InfoNCE objective, whose optimization can prematurely saturate under a strong pre-trained initialization: on dense captions, the loss falls below 10^-3 on 80% of batches within the first epoch, while its gradient becomes numerically zero in 47% of measurements. We find that this behavior is closely related to the large number of near-duplicate captions in dense-caption benchmarks,
